To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the role of personal attributes (PA) in the genesis and/or progression of lung disease is not clear; (2) the role of PA in smoking initiation and maintenance is not clear; and (3) there are several methodological issues that must be addressed before PA research can make a significant contribution to understanding lung disease and cigarette use.

(i) the personal characteristics of smokers and nonsmokers are different, (ii) these differences are present in early adolescence, (iii) these differences are related to smoking, and (iv) these differences are also related to lung function and lung disease.

the role of personal attributes (i.e., personality traits and psychological factors) in the genesis and progress of lung disease is limited and that the role of these personal attributes in the progression of cigarette smoking is limited and is not a major determinant of smoking status.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of personal attributes (i.e., personality traits and social cognitions) in the genesis and maintenance of lung disease and in the genesis and persistence of cigarette smoking.
the role of individual characteristics in the development and progression of lung diseases.
the role that personal attributes play in the genesis and/or progression of lung disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
smoking is a major risk factor for the development of COPD, but that the risk is influenced by genetic factors, and by the interaction of genetic factors with environmental factors.
smoking causes lung cancer and other diseases of the lungs, including emphysema.
there is a relationship between the use of cigarettes and the development of lung disease and cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of personality in the genesis and/or progression of chronic lung disease is unclear.
the role of individual attributes in the development and progression of lung illness and cigarette smoking is complex and not yet completely understood.
the results suggest a significant part of the variance in the development of lung disease is explained by the interaction of individual attributes, smoking behavior, and the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a novel method of identifying the most important features in the data, in our case, the features that are most important in predicting lung disease progression and the most important features that are most associated with cigarette smoking.
personal characteristics such as personality and cognitive ability are associated with smoking and lung disease.
personal attributes, such as age, race, sex, and education, are important factors that influence the development of lung disease and smoking behavior.
